findings.description: storage_encrypted is set to false, so the RDS MySQL instance stores all data unencrypted on disk, including any snapshots. Sensitive application data is exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the RDS instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, greatly enlarging the attack surface for a database holding application data and protected only by MySQL credentials.

The master username is the default 'admin' and the password is supplied via a plain Terraform variable, which is stored unencrypted in state and echoed into EC2 user data; combined with the public endpoint this is a direct credential exposure path.
The instance uses a parameter group that does not set require_secure_transport (or equivalent SSL enforcement), so MySQL clients may connect over cleartext to a publicly accessible endpoint.

findings.issue_category: TLS not enforced in parameter group
findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group defines only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport=1, leaving unencrypted database connections permitted.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the EC2 instance role. An attacker who compromises the internet-facing web instance can read or destroy all S3 data, modify RDS, and manipulate EC2 across the account, including privilege-escalation via instance/role manipulation.

The user_data script writes the RDS master username and password in cleartext into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable from the instance metadata service by any process or SSRF on the host and is visible in the AWS console/API.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled on an internet-facing web server whose instance profile holds wildcard S3/EC2/RDS permissions, making SSRF-based credential theft trivial.
No root_block_device/ebs encryption configuration is declared, so the instance volume containing the plaintext database credentials file may be stored unencrypted.

The bootstrap script installs and serves the credential-handling PHP application over plain HTTP (httpd with no TLS configuration), so form submissions and query results traverse the network unencrypted.

Egress allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, permitting unrestricted outbound connections that facilitate data exfiltration or command-and-control from a compromised host.

The RDS security group has no description and, paired with a publicly accessible database instance, its VPC-CIDR ingress rule provides no effective boundary against the public endpoint that bypasses subnet isolation.
